column1: # Real-world phrasings against expected answer slugs.
# The bank's own `answer_questions` cannot measure the matcher: those are the
# strings it is indexed on, so scoring against them measures nothing but that
# the index works. These are how people actually type — lowercase, unpunctuated,
# colloquial, often first-person — which is the only version of the question
# the matcher will ever see in production.
# Column 2 is the acceptable answer, or several separated by `|` where more
# than one would genuinely serve the reader. `-` means the bank has no answer
# and an honest miss is the correct behaviour.
# Two rules keep this honest:
#   Never add one of these strings to `content/questions.yaml` as a phrasing.
#   The bank is indexed on its phrasings, so a question copied into it stops
#   measuring anything and starts measuring itself. Where the eval exposes a
#   phrasing gap, fix it with a different wording of the same intent — and
#   expect the score here to flatter the fix afterwards, which is what
#   `heldout.tsv` is for.
#   When the eval and the bank disagree, check which one is wrong. "can i pray
#   without covering my hair" is marked `-` because the bank holds
#   `awrah-for-men` and nothing at all on a woman's covering in prayer — the
#   expectation was wrong and the gap is real, and both are worth writing down.
